rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ship belonged to ten impoverished brothers, five disabled; they hired it out at sea because they could not resist oppressors. Collective attribution either uses grammatical predominance or treats agents’ work as the principals’ work.
rows.anchor: وكانوا عشرة إخوة خمسة منهم زمنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Hanafi and Shafi‘i law, the terms are reversed: a poor person owns less than the 200-dirham threshold beyond necessities, while a miskin owns nothing; the Hanafi definition is the sound one.
rows.anchor: هذا هو الصحيح عند الحنفية والشافعية يعكسون

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: The verse shows that miskin can mean someone who owns something insufficient for his needs, taking the lām as indicating ownership.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي في الآية دليل أن المسكين يطلق على من يملك شيئا لم يكفه

rows.speaker: مولانا سعدي
rows.claim: Sa‘di says the ownership inference works only if the ship was theirs; its lām could instead indicate association through a loan or their employment, as a report says.
rows.anchor: قال مولانا سعدي : إنما يكون دليلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if they owned the ship, they are called miskin because disability and helplessness before the tyrant humiliated them; this is not the technical miskin eligible for alms.
rows.anchor: لعجزهم عن دفع الملك الظالم ولزمانتهم والمسكين يقع على من أذله شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khidr’s ‘I wanted’ means by God’s judgment and will, and ‘damage it’ means to make it defective.
rows.anchor: فأردت} بحكم الله وإرادته {أن أعيبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here warāʾ means ahead of them, an opposite sense of the word, supported by the subsequent story; the king seized every sound, fine ship, with ‘seizing’ parsed as a verbal noun or circumstantial phrase.
rows.anchor: ورآءهم} أمامهم كقوله : ومن ورائهم برزخ فوراء من الأضداد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The infidel king was Jalandi son of Karkard, in Cordoba in al-Andalus; Abu al-Layth says the first corruption at sea was his tyranny, while the first on land was Cain’s killing of Abel.
rows.anchor: اسمه جلندي بن كركرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat of confiscation explains the damage; it is mentioned after the intention to foreground that the hole was meant to spoil the ship, not drown its passengers, answering Moses’ objection.
rows.anchor: الخرق لقصد التعييب لا لقصد الإغراق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khidr apologized to the owners and explained the predatory king, whose plan they had not known.
rows.anchor: وروي أن الخضر اعتذر إلى القوم وذكر لهم شأن الملك الغاصب ولم يكونوا يعلمون بخبره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Prophets’ Stories account says the king’s troops checked the ship, found the missing plank and left; after they departed, Khidr replaced it.
rows.anchor: فوجدوا موضع اللوح مفتوحا فانصرفوا فلما بعدوا عنهم أخذ الخضر ذلك اللوح ورده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Mathnawi’s examples present apparent destruction as repair: breaking, dismantling, or painful treatment can make rebuilding, healing, and flourishing possible.
rows.anchor: فظاهر فعله تخريب وباطنه تعمير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Effacing metaphorical existence yields real existence; while human nature and its traits remain, divine qualities cannot manifest.
rows.anchor: وفي إفناء الوجود المجازي تحصيل للوجود الحقيقي فما دامت البشرية وأوصافها باقية

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The inward reading says damaging the ship to avert seizure is impermissible under outward law but allowed by inward law for its owner’s benefit; it extends this to a realized jurist judging by a greater inward good consistent with reality.
rows.anchor: خرق السفينة وإعابتها لئلا تؤخذ غصبا ليس من أحكام الشرع ظاهرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The slain boy was Jaisur; his parents were named Kazbara and Suhwa in al-Ta‘rif. Their faith meant affirming God’s oneness.
rows.anchor: وهو جيسور {فكان أبواه} اسم أبيه كازبرا واسم أمه سهوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khashiya here means fearing that the boy would overwhelm his parents with misguidance and disbelief; the Sheikh explains they might follow him through their love and abandon faith.
rows.anchor: أي : يكلفهما {طغيانا} ضلالة {وكفرا} ويتبعان له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khidr feared this because God informed him the child was created with an unbelieving disposition.
rows.anchor: لأن الله أعلمه بحال الولد أنه طبع أي : خلق كافرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The replacement would be a child purer from sins and bad traits, and more compassionate and dutiful toward the parents.
rows.anchor: خيرا منه زكواة} طهارة من الذنوب والأخلاق الرديئة {وأقرب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ‘Abbas says God replaced the boy with a girl who married a prophet and bore seventy prophets.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أبدلهما الله جارية تزوجها نبي من الأنبياء فولدت سبعين نبيا

rows.speaker: مطرف
rows.claim: Mutarrif says the parents rejoiced at the child’s birth and grieved at his killing; had he lived, he would have destroyed them. A believer should accept God’s decree as better than personal preference.
rows.anchor: قال مطرف فرح به أبواه حين ولد وحزنا عليه حين قتل ولو بقي لكان فيه هلاكهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An apparent enemy can inwardly be a loving helper, and a quarrelsome critic may benefit more by exposing faults than a flattering friend who hides them.
rows.anchor: فرب عداوة هي في الحقيقة محبة ورب عدو هو في الباطن محب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A preacher prayed for highway robbers because they had driven him from trade toward the path of the poor and worship; their harm became the cause of his spiritual turning.
rows.anchor: وكان واعظ كلما وعظ ودعا أشرك في دعائه قطاع الطريق

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Killing an innocent is forbidden by outward law, but inwardly permitted to someone granted disclosure of outcomes when the child’s life would corrupt his parents’ faith and complete his own misery.
rows.anchor: قتل النفس الزكية بلا جرم منها محظور في ظاهر الشرع وإن كان فيه مصلحة لغيره

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The episode illustrates 2:216: the parents hated the killing though it benefited them, loved the child’s life though it harmed them, and the boy’s own wish to live would have led to greater misery.
rows.anchor: تحقيق قوله تعالى : {وعسى أن تكرهوا شيئا وهو خير لكم}

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: If God removes a harmful beloved thing from a believer who is patient and grateful, He replaces it with something better, beneficial, and harmless.
rows.anchor: إذا أخذ من العبد المؤمن شيئا من محبوباته وهو مضر له والعبد غافل عن مضرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prays to be among those patient and grateful in sacred law and the spiritual path, and to reach what is better and more complete in reality.
rows.anchor: نسأل الله تعالى أن يجعلنا من الصابرين الشاكرين في الشريعة والطريقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The orphans were Asram and Sarim, sons of Kashih; their father Siyaha was a pious traveler, and their mother was Dunya according to al-Naqqash. The city was Antioch.
rows.anchor: اسمهما اصرم وصريم ابنا كاشح وكان سياحا تقيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent report says the treasure was buried gold and silver, transmitted from the Prophet; this fits the condemnation of hoarding when dues are unpaid.
rows.anchor: أي مال مدفون لهما من ذهب وفضة روى ذلك مرفوعا وهو الظاهر

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: An alternative says the treasure was a gold or marble tablet of maxims: trust providence rather than grieve or toil anxiously, remember death and judgment rather than indulge worldly life, and know God creates good and evil.
rows.anchor: وهو قول الجمهور كما في

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People entrusted valuables to the righteous father and received them safely; the boys’ property and persons were protected because of his righteousness.
rows.anchor: كان الناس يضعون الودائع عند ذلك الصالح فيردها إليهم سالمة فحفظا بصلاح أبيهما

rows.speaker: جعفر بن محمد
rows.claim: Ja‘far ibn Muhammad says seven generations separated the boys from their righteous ancestor, the seventh forefather who buried the treasure.
rows.anchor: قال جعفر بن محمد : كان بينهما وبين الأب الصالح سبعة آباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The boys were to reach maturity, described as puberty and sound judgment; reports differ on its precise age, ending at thirty-three or eighteen.
rows.anchor: الأشد في معنى القوة جمع شدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun shifts are explained by each act’s moral character: Khidr takes apparent blame for the ship, uses ‘we’ for feared disbelief, and ascribes the pure good of maturity only to God.
rows.anchor: فالأول في نفسه شر قبيح والثالث خير محض والثاني ممتزج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation asks who Khidr was to will the first act, then includes Moses in ‘we willed,’ but assigns the third will to God alone, without claiming a share in it.
rows.anchor: فخص في الثالثة الإرادة بالله أي : دون إضافة الإرادة إلى نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without the repaired wall it would have fallen before the boys could preserve or grow the wealth, and the treasure would have been lost.
rows.anchor: لولا أني أقمته لانقض وخرج الكنز من تحته قبل اقتدارهما على حفظ المال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Imam’s answer to the puzzle of how the boys could find the treasure is that they did not know it and their guardian was away.
rows.anchor: لعلهما لم يعلماه وعلم القيم إلا أنه كان غائبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says the puzzle is no objection: God could guide them to it, discoveries without prior knowledge are common, and the lām grants them the exclusive right to find it; a seventh-generation ancestor could hardly have buried it for them.
rows.anchor: لأن الله تعالى قادر على أن يعرفهما مكان ذلك الكنز بطريق من الطرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rahmatan min rabbik may be a circumstantial phrase meaning ‘shown mercy,’ a reason for the divine will, or an omitted verb meaning God had mercy on them.
rows.anchor: {رحمة من ربك} لهما مصدر في موقع الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khidr says the ship, killing, and wall were not his own judgment but God’s command and revelation; this explains the troubling acts to Moses and models a compassionate guide dispelling a student’s doubts.
rows.anchor: ما فعلت ما رأيته يا موسى من خرق السفينة وقتل الغلام وإقامة الجدار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘That’ refers to the consequences, and ‘what you could not bear patiently’ completes the promised explanation.
rows.anchor: المذكور من العواقب {تأويل ما لم تسطع

rows.speaker: بعض العارفين
rows.claim: A gnostic warns that lacking any share of bestowed, unveiled knowledge risks a bad end; its minimum share is to affirm it and submit to its people, while denial bars one from it.
rows.anchor: قال بعض العارفين : من لم يكن له نصيب من هذا العلم

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: God’s wisdom and mercy employ two prophets, Moses and Khidr, for the welfare of the two children.
rows.anchor: يستعمل نبيين مثل موسى والخضر عليهما السلام في مصلحة الطفلين

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Prophets may pursue worldly matters when they serve an otherworldly good, especially a benefit to someone else for God’s sake.
rows.anchor: مثل الأنبياء يجوز أن يسعى في أمر دنيوي إذا كان فيه صلاح أمر أخروي

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: God protects a people and their descendants through a righteous person, extending blessings as far as the seventh generation.
rows.anchor: يحفظ بصالح قوما وقبيلة ويوصل بركاته إلى البطن السابع

rows.speaker: محمد بن المنكدر
rows.claim: Ibn al-Munkadir says God protects a righteous person’s children, grandchildren, clan, and nearby households in His shelter.
rows.anchor: قال محمد بن المنكدر إن الله يحفظ بالرجل الصالح ولده وولد ولده وعشيرته

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: Sa‘id ibn al-Musayyib says that when he prays and remembers his child, he lengthens his prayer.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد بن المسيب إني أصلي وأذكر ولدي فأزيد في صلاتي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A sound report from Ibn ‘Abbas says the boys were preserved through their father’s righteousness; if this benefited descendants seven generations later, the Prophet’s pure family has even greater claim to blessing.
rows.anchor: وصح عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṣawa‘iq says sanctuary pigeons were honored as descendants of the pair that nested at the Thawr cave while the Prophet hid there during the Hijra.
rows.anchor: إن حمام الحرم إنما أكرم لأنه من ذرية حمامتين عششتا على غار ثور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In al-‘Ara’is, an Alid whom Harun al-Rashid meant to kill says he prayed, ‘Preserve me through my ancestors as You preserved the treasure for the boys through their father.’
rows.anchor: يا من حفظ الكنز على الصبيين لصلاح أبيهما احفظني لصلاح آبائي

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: A disciple should obey the shaykh, act only for God, and avoid worldly greed or egoistic aims that ruin the deed and sever companionship.
rows.anchor: ليتأدب المريد فيما استعمله الشيخ وينقاد له ولا يعمل إلا لوجه الله

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: God preserves a righteous servant’s rightful wealth when its preservation serves a good purpose.
rows.anchor: أن الله تعالى يحفظ المال الصالح للعبد الصالح إذا كان فيه صلاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everything involving prophets and saints happens by God’s command inwardly and outwardly: Khidr acted under an explicit command, while Moses objected in keeping with the outward law because he lacked the inward instruction.
rows.anchor: أي : فعلته بأمر ربي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Patience with a shaykh’s actions is difficult; excuse, forgive, and overlook a sincere disciple’s mistakes or objections up to three times, after which separation is excusable and the shaykh should explain the matter.
rows.anchor: فليعذره ويعف عنه ويتجاوز إلى ثلاث مرات

rows.speaker: العوارف
rows.claim: The disciple should inwardly clear the shaykh of suspicion in all his actions; objection poisons discipleship, and the Moses–Khidr story teaches that apparently wrong acts may prove sound when their reasons are disclosed.
rows.anchor: ويحذر المريد الاعتراض على الشيخ ويزيل اتهام الشيخ عن باطنه

rows.speaker: الحافظ
rows.claim: Hafez’s couplet advises listening to sincere counsel and accepting it without excuses.
rows.anchor: نصيحتي كنمت بشنو وبهانه مكير هر آنكه ناصح مشفق بكويدت بذير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A spiritual guide should be realized and compassionate, not an unfeeling imitator, lest followers’ efforts be wasted.
rows.anchor: وينبغي أن يكون المرشد محققا ومشفقا لا مقلدا غير مشفق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An Arabic verse warns that if a crow guides people, it will lead them to a place of carrion.
rows.anchor: إذا كان الغراب دليل قوم سيهديهم إلى أرض الجياف

rows.speaker: الحافظ
rows.claim: Hafez says concealed pain may be better than seeking cures from pretentious physicians, who might instead receive a remedy from the unseen treasury.
rows.anchor: دردم نهفته به زطبيبان مدعى

rows.speaker: الصائب
rows.claim: Sa’ib likens seeking one’s cure from the same source of pain to pulling out a thorn with a scorpion’s stinger.
rows.anchor: ربي دردان علاج درد خودجستن بآن ماند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When two harms conflict, bear the lesser to avert the greater, though legal schools may differ on details.
rows.anchor: إذا تعارض ضرران يجب تحمل أهونهما لدفع أعظمهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Examples include praying seated with gestures to preserve ritual purity when prostration would reopen a wound, and praying seated with recitation when standing prevents recitation.
rows.anchor: يصلي قاعدا يومي بالركوع والسجود لأن ترك الركوع والسجود أهون

rows.speaker: ابن نجيم
rows.claim: For a man who cannot stand at the congregation but can stand at home, al-Khulasa says he prays seated; Sharh al-Munya says at home standing, which Ibn Nujaym calls the clearer view.
rows.anchor: قال ابن نجيم وهو الأظهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In necessity, a person should eat carrion rather than take someone else’s property.
rows.anchor: ومن اضطر وعنده ميتة ومال الغير أكلها دونه

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: If forced to jump into deadly fire or from a mountain, the Imam says choose the option one judges less harmful; his two companions say endure until killed.
rows.anchor: عند الإمام وعندهما يصبر حتى يقتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The questioners were Jews testing the Prophet about a man who traveled to the ends of east and west; alternatively Quraysh asked at their prompting.
rows.anchor: هم اليهود سألوه على وجه الامتحان عن رجل طواف

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says four people ruled the earth: believers Solomon and Dhu al-Qarnayn, and unbelievers Nimrod and Nebuchadnezzar; Mishkat al-Anwar gives Shaddad son of ‘Ad instead of Nebuchadnezzar.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد ملك الأرض أربعة مؤمنان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports place Dhu al-Qarnayn after Nimrod in Abraham’s era or after Thamud; the Sheikh says Khidr led his vanguard like a royal vizier. One account gives his life as 1,600 years.
rows.anchor: وكان ذو القرنين بعد نمرود في عهد إبراهيم عليه السلام

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir calls him a righteous, just ruler who conquered regions and kings, died at Shahrazur on returning from the darkness, and was buried there; the text inconsistently says he was neither prophet nor king before calling him a king.
rows.anchor: والصحيح أنه ما كان نبيا ولا ملكا وإنما كان ملكا صالحا عادلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tibyan says his journey around the world lasted five hundred, and after building the barrier he returned to Jerusalem and died there.
rows.anchor: مدة دوران ذي القرنين في الدنيا خمسمائة ولما فرغ من بناء السد رجع إلى بيت المقدس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He was called Dhu al-Qarnayn because he reached the sun’s two horns, meaning its eastern and western extremes; Ardshir was called long-armed because his command reached wherever he wished.
rows.anchor: وإنما سمي بذي القرنين لأنه بلغ قرني الشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qamus says Dhu al-Qarnayn was killed by blows to his right and then left horn while preaching, and revived by God both times.
rows.anchor: لما دعاهم إلى الله ضربوه على قرنه الأيمن فمات فأحياه الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A story says Ali was called Dhu al-Qarnayn because he received two head wounds, from ‘Amr ibn ‘Abd Wudd and Ibn Muljam.
rows.anchor: كما سمي علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه بذي القرنين لما كان شجتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophets’ Stories says he dreamed of approaching the sun and taking its horns in east and west, after which his people named him for the dream.
rows.anchor: وكان قد رأى في منامه أنه دنا من الشمس حتى أخذ بقرنيها

rows.speaker: السيوطي
rows.claim: Al-Suyuti’s tale says he was the first to wear a turban to hide two moving horns; when his scribe leaked the secret through reeds that became talking flutes, the king accepted that God meant it to be known.
rows.anchor: أول من لبس العمامة ذو القرنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’anic Dhu al-Qarnayn is the earlier, righteous ruler, not the later Roman Alexander: the latter lived over two millennia later, before Christ, fought Darius, and was an unbeliever; scholars often confused them.
rows.anchor: فالمراد بذي القرنين في القرآن هو الأول دون الثاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The answer promises a definite account: ‘I will recite’ means explain their requested report or recite revelation about him, with the future particle reinforcing certainty.
rows.anchor: والسين للتأكيد والدلالة على التحقق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tamkin means empowering and preparing means, so no direct object is needed; making someone capable and making power available to him are near in meaning and can interchange, as in 6:6.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الأول جعله قادرا قويا ومعنى الثاني جعل له قدرة وقوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gave Dhu al-Qarnayn command of clouds, light, and darkness and made travel easy; a report says he dismounted and walked to greet Abraham at Mecca, after which clouds carried him, his army, and equipment.
rows.anchor: فنزل ذو القرنين ومشى إلى إبراهيم فسلم عليه إبراهيم واعتنقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report says Dhu al-Qarnayn was the first to embrace when greeting; light guided him from the front and darkness shielded him behind.
rows.anchor: فكانت السحاب تحمله وعساكره وجميع آلاتهم إذا أرادوا غزوة قوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sabab is a route to a goal, including any means of reaching it such as knowledge, power, or a tool; he followed and pursued the route toward the west.
rows.anchor: طريقا يوصل إليه وهو كل ما يتوصل به إلى المقصود من علم أو قدرة أو آلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ittaba‘a implies catching up with a predecessor, unlike taba‘a, simply going along; Pharaoh ‘followed’ Moses in the pursuing sense (10:90).
rows.anchor: يقال تبعه اتباعا إذا طلب الثاني اللحوق بالأول وتبعه تبعا إذا مر به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Irshad speculates he first headed west to honor the sun; al-Tibyan says he sought the spring of life by the Sea of Darkness after hearing it lay there.
rows.anchor: قصد إلى ناحية المغرب يطلب عين الحياة

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The inward reading says questioners should not be turned away and stories strengthen hearts; Dhu al-Qarnayn’s empowerment signifies divine caliphate, making every divine potential act possible through him and subjecting the world to him.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" يشير بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His westward journey symbolizes the order of spiritual ascent: bodily realms must be traversed before rising to the world of spirits and reality.
rows.anchor: فإن المغرب إشارة إلى الأجسام والمشرق إلى الأرواح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He reached the western edge of inhabited land at the shore of the encircling sea; the Sheikh says he reached people with no one beyond them, since no one can reach the sun’s actual setting place.
rows.anchor: إلى منتهى الأرض من جهة المغرب بحيث لا يتمكن أحد من مجاوزته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In al-Tibyan’s spring-of-life tale, the guide recommends female horses and then unbroken mares for travel through the darkness; Khidr, at the vanguard, finds and drinks from the spring while Dhu al-Qarnayn fails.
rows.anchor: فجمع من عسكره ستة آلاف فرس كذلك فركبوا الرماك وترك بقية عسكره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A muddy spring is a pool of black mud by etymology; from the sea’s edge, the sun only appears to sink into water because no farther shore is visible, so the verse says ‘he found it setting.’
rows.anchor: إذ ليس في مطمح نظره غير الماء كراكب البحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some describe a last inhabited place where the sun appeared to sink into a dark hollow; actually it sets beyond the sea, since the earth is spherical, the sky surrounds it, and the sun in its orbit is many times larger than Earth.
rows.anchor: أن الأرض كرة والسماء محيطة بها والشمس في الفلك

rows.speaker: السمرقندي
rows.claim: Al-Samarqandi raises a hadith saying the sun is in the fourth heaven and vast, then answers that God can place all seven heavens and earths in something tiny, so a spring poses no limit to divine power.
rows.anchor: قال السمرقندي رحمه الله في

rows.speaker: التأويلات
rows.claim: The inward commentary says the verse reports Dhu al-Qarnayn’s perception, not the sun’s literal entry into a pool: from a ship at the sea’s impassable limit it looked as if it set in the spring.
rows.anchor: إن الله تعالى لم يخبر عن حقيقة غروبها في عين حمئة وإنما أخبر عن وجدان ذي القرنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say a prophet would see things as they are, like the Prophet seeing the Negus from Medina and praying over him; if Dhu al-Qarnayn was not a prophet, the sight was according to his assumption.
rows.anchor: إذا كان ذو القرنين نبيا فنظر النبي ثاقب يرى الأشياء على ما هي عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Near it’ means the sea shore at the end of inhabited land; reports describe a twelve-thousand-gate city whose noise obscured the sun, or Jabulsa/Jirjisa with ten thousand gates, descendants of believing Thamud who accepted the Prophet during the Night Journey.
rows.anchor: وقال الإمام السهيلي : هم أهل جابلص بالفتح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Questions of Wisdom says reports about Jabalqa and Jabalsa and their people’s belief on the Night Journey are well known.
rows.anchor: أما حديث جابلصا وجابلقا وايمان أهاليهما ليلة المعراج

rows.speaker: التأويلات
rows.claim: The inward commentary takes God’s command to Dhu al-Qarnayn to fight as evidence of his prophethood, citing the Prophetic instruction to fight people until they profess God’s oneness.
rows.anchor: ويدل على نبوته كونه مأمورا بالقتال معهم

rows.speaker: الحدادي
rows.claim: Al-Haddadi objects that prophethood cannot be established without definitive proof.
rows.anchor: قال الحدادي : لا يمكن إثبات نبوة إلا بدليل قطعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After calling them to Islam, Dhu al-Qarnayn may punish rejecters by killing or treat them well through pardon or captivity; alternatively, the two outcomes are assigned respectively to persistent rejecters and those who repent.
rows.anchor: إما تعذيبك بالقتل إن أبوا وإما إحسانك بالعفو أو الأسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wrongdoer is one who persists in unbelief and rejects Dhu al-Qarnayn’s call; Dhu al-Qarnayn and his followers punish him in this world by killing him, then he returns to God for unprecedented punishment in Hell.
rows.anchor: {ظلم} نفسه بالإصرار على الكفر ولم يقبل الإيمان مني

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada reports that unbelievers were cooked in cauldrons, while believers were given clothing and gifts.
rows.anchor: وعن قتادة كان يطبخ من كفر في القدور ومن آمن أعطاه وكساه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A believer who accepts the call and acts rightly receives the good reward in both worlds, understood as good recompense or Paradise; Dhu al-Qarnayn promises commands that are easy and not burdensome.
rows.anchor: أي : فله المثوبة الحسنى حال كونه مجزيا بها

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Al-Kashifi recounts that a people overwhelmed by the army of darkness pleaded for safety and believed.
rows.anchor: آورده اندكه لشكر ظلمت مرا برقوم ناسك كاشت تابكوش ودهن در آمد وزنهار خواستند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Prophets’ Stories account says he called each people to God, accepted converts, and enveloped rejecters in darkness until they submitted; after eight days and nights he reached Mount Qaf, where an angel said it encircles the earth and prevents it overturning.
rows.anchor: فلا يمر بأمة إلا دعاها إلى الله تعالى فإن أجابوه قبل منهم وإن لم يجيبوه غشيتهم الظلمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angel advises him not to worry over tomorrow’s provision, delay today’s work, grieve what is lost, act gently, or become tyrannical and proud.
rows.anchor: يا ذا القرنين لا يهمنك رزق غد ، ولا تؤخر عمل اليوم لغد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Persian counsel says pride makes a ruler lose dignity and harm the people; one should discipline oneself and avoid striking people’s minds with harshness.
rows.anchor: تكبر كند مرد حشمت رست نداندكه حشمت بحلم اندرست

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He then followed a route back from the west toward the east.
rows.anchor: تبع وسلك طريقا راجعا من مغرب الشمس موصلا إلى مشرقها

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Al-Kashifi says he brought the Nasik people with him, sent the army of light ahead, left the army of darkness behind, subdued the people of Hawil, and set out east.
rows.anchor: قوم تماسك را باخودبرده لشكر نوررا زيش روان كرد وعسكر ظلمت را

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sunrise point means the first inhabited region in the east; he could not literally reach where the sun rises. Reports give twelve years or less for the journey, aided by clouds and facilitated routes.
rows.anchor: يعني الموضع الذي تطلع عليه الشمس أولا من معمورة الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The eastern people were naked, without clothing or buildings for shade because their soil could not hold structures; they escaped underground or into the sea during the heat, then caught fish and cooked them in the sun.
rows.anchor: ليس لهم لباس يتسترون به من حر الشمس ولا بناء يستظلون فيه

rows.speaker: الحدادي
rows.claim: Al-Haddadi says they had no head or body hair or eyebrows and looked flayed because of their region’s extreme heat.
rows.anchor: قال الحدادي : ليس على رؤوسهم ولا على أجسادهم شعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed traveler beyond China says the people sheltered him after a loud ringing made him faint; at sunrise the water looked like oil, and they later fished in the sea and cooked fish in sunlight.
rows.anchor: فلما طلعت الشمس على الماء إذ هو فوق الماء كهيئة الزيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Thus’ refers either to Dhu al-Qarnayn’s exalted rank and broad dominion, or to governing the eastern people as he had the western people, with their choice of treatment.
rows.anchor: أي : أمر ذي القرنين كما وصفناه لك في رفعة المحل

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Al-Kashifi says he treated the eastern people as he had the western ones and continued to another people called Ta’wil.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (همنان كرد اسكندر با يشان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God fully knew all Dhu al-Qarnayn possessed, outwardly and inwardly; khubran is an accusative of specification meaning knowledge of visible and hidden matters.
rows.anchor: تمييز أي : علما تعلق بظواهره وخفاياه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wahb ibn Munabbih describes Dhu al-Qarnayn as an Alexandrian woman’s only son, without noble ancestry, who grew into a chaste, capable, and virtuous man, became renowned, chose Islam, and brought his people to it by force.
rows.anchor: ذكر وهب بن منبه أن ذا القرنين كان رجلا من أهل الاسكندرية ابن امرأة عجوز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says his just conquests succeeded although earlier kings had greater treasuries and armies: by God’s help he did not wrong subjects or speak ill of former rulers.
rows.anchor: بعون خداى عز وجل كه هر مملكت راكه كرفتم رعيتش را نيازردم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Persian verse says wisdom honors a person through good conduct and lowers him through injustice; another says no one can undo the prayer of an oppressed victim.
rows.anchor: بزركش نحو انند اهل خرد كه نام برز كان بزشتى برد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tibyan offers a contrasting story: a proud, tyrannical heir imprisoned a righteous adviser, but divine rescue and fire made him recognize his weakness, repent, and rule justly; he then built a large mosque.
rows.anchor: كان أي : ذو القرنين ملكا جبارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He followed a third route running crosswise between east and west, from south toward north.
rows.anchor: أخذ طريقا ثالثا معترضا بين المشرق والمغرب آخذا من الجنوب إلى الشمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two barriers are tall mountains at the far eastern edge of Turkic lands, with Gog and Magog beyond them.
rows.anchor: جبلان عاليان في منقطع أرض الترك مما يلي المشرق من ورائهما يأجوج ومأجوج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sadd with a fatḥa can mean a human-made barrier and with a ḍamma a natural one; both can mean mountain or obstruction. Bayna functions as a direct object here but also occurs as a noun, adverb, or in a genitive construction.
rows.anchor: بالفتح ما كان من عمل الخلق وبالضم ما كان من خلق الله

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Al-Kashifi, like al-Jalalayn, construes ‘before them’ as ‘near the two mountains.’
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (يافت دريش آن دوكوه)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people could scarcely understand others’ speech, and others could not understand their strange language; al-Zamakhshari says they understood only with great effort and gestures, like deaf-mutes, and identifies them as Turks.
rows.anchor: لا يفهمون كلام أحد ولا يفهم الناس كلامهم لغرابة لغتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Historians trace Arabs, Persians, and Romans to Shem; Africans to Ham; Turks, Khazars, Slavs, and Gog and Magog to Japheth. Anwar al-Mashariq instead traces Turks to Ibrahim’s children by Qantura.
rows.anchor: ويافث أبو الترك والخزر والصقالبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They spoke through an interpreter, apparently because Dhu al-Qarnayn had been given knowledge of languages.
rows.anchor: على لسان ترجمانهم بطريق الشكاية والظاهر أن ذى القرنين كان قد أوتي اللغات

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The apparent tension between scarcely understanding speech and speaking is resolved because negative yakādu can indicate that something almost fails yet does occur; they understood enough by divine inspiration to make their plea persuasive.
rows.anchor: لا يفقهون قولا يلين به قلب ذي القرنين ليجعل لهم السد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yajuj and Majuj are either foreign names, or Arabic feminine proper names of two tribes descended from Japheth; another account makes them descendants of Adam’s wet dream, without a mother.
rows.anchor: أن آدم احتلم ذات يوم وامتزجت نطفته بالتراب فهم منها

rows.speaker: أنوار المشارق
rows.claim: Anwar al-Mashariq rejects the Adam origin as baseless; Bahr al-‘Ulum also says it contradicts the report that no prophet ever had a wet dream.
rows.anchor: وقال في "أنوار المشارق" هذا منكر جدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author’s sheikh taught that Adam was the first afflicted with a wet dream for a hidden wisdom; the hadith excludes prophets other than Adam, and restraint in discussing it is for reverence.
rows.anchor: سمعت من فم حضرة شيخي وسندي روح الله روحه أنه قال في أول من ابتلي بالاحتلام أبونا آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gog and Magog devastate the land by killing, destruction, and consuming crops; in spring they eat everything green or dry, sometimes people, and each lives to see a thousand armed sons. Ibn ‘Abbas says they are a tenth of humankind.
rows.anchor: وكانوا يخرجون أيام الربيع فلا يتركون أخضر إلا أكلوه ولا يابسا إلا احتملوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports describe three Gog-and-Magog types: giants 120 cubits tall, tiny people the height and width of a handspan, and huge-eared people; they are hairy, howl, reproduce like beasts, and devour animals, corpses, insects, snakes, and scorpions.
rows.anchor: صنف منهم طول الرجل منهم مائة وعشرون ذراعا وصنف منهم قد هم على شبر واحد طولهم وعرضهم سواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hayat al-Hayawan describes a giant red-eyed dragon: first a land serpent, then cast into the sea, where it grows enormous and devours sea creatures; God eventually sends an angel to Gog and Magog with it.
rows.anchor: التنين ضرب من الحياة كأكبر ما يكون فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophets’ Stories says they prosper when the dragon is cast to them and suffer famine when it is not.
rows.anchor: إذا قذفوا بها خصبوا وإلا قحطوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kharj may mean payment, synonymous with kharaj, or the two can be distinguished by whether the levy is on land, a person, voluntary, or obligatory.
rows.anchor: والخرج والخراج واحد كالنول والنوال أو الخراج ما على الأرض والذمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people offer a payment for building a barrier that will stop Gog and Magog reaching them.
rows.anchor: جعلا من أموالنا أي : أجرا نخرجه لك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading of makkannī is either assimilated or unassimilated; it means God gave Dhu al-Qarnayn access and power through kingship, wealth, and other means. Those gifts are better than the tribute offered, which he does not need.
rows.anchor: بالادغام وقرىء بالفك أي : الذي مكنني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He asks them for capable workers and tools instead, and promises a massive, layered, fortified barrier, stronger than an ordinary obstruction and beyond their expectations.
rows.anchor: بفعلة وصناع يحسنون البناء والعمل بآلات لا بد منها في البناء

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The inward reading takes iron blocks as the requested ‘strength,’ meaning provision of tools; this does not contradict refusal of tribute because they provide or buy materials rather than pay a levy for labor.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى : {زبر الحديدا حتى} تفسير للقوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Stories say they mined iron and copper; one account dug a thousand steps between the mountains down to water, while other reports give a three-mile gap or a hundred parasangs, with rock and copper foundations and wood and charcoal layers. One description makes it 200 cubits high and 50 wide.
rows.anchor: قاس ما بين الصدفين فوجده ثلاثة أميال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sadaf means the mountain’s edge or side; he filled the space until the wall matched the mountains in height and set bellows around it.
rows.anchor: الصدف منقطع الجبل أو ناحيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Workers blew on the iron until it became fire-hot; the copper crew brought molten copper for Dhu al-Qarnayn to pour over it. Attributing the heating to him emphasizes that he directed the work.
rows.anchor: للذين يتولون أمر النحاس من الإذابة ونحوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first verb drops the tāʾ for ease and to avoid adjacent similar sounds; al-Burhan says deletion suits its complex verbal object, while the second retains it because its object is the single noun ‘breach.’
rows.anchor: اختار التخفيف في الأول لأن مفعوله حرف وفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the copper fused with the iron, Gog and Magog could neither climb the high, smooth barrier nor breach its thick, hard base.
rows.anchor: أي : وما قدروا أن ينقبوه ويخرقوه من أسفله

rows.speaker: الإرشاد
rows.claim: The extraordinary work is a miracle: God protected the workers from extreme heat while they blew on and poured metal over the heated blocks.
rows.anchor: فكأنه سبحانه صرف تأثير تلك الحرارة العظيمة عن أبدان أولئك المباشرين للأعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author suggests they may have blown and poured from a distance by ingenious means, as Nimrod’s people used a catapult to throw Abraham into a fire no one could approach.
rows.anchor: ليس ببعيد أن يكون المباشرة بالنفخ والصب من بعيد بطريق من طرق الحيل

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A man who saw the barrier described it to the Prophet as embroidered cloth, with black and red stripes; the Prophet said he had seen it, the colors being iron and copper.
rows.anchor: وعن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن رجلا أخبره به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhu al-Qarnayn calls the barrier a great mercy and blessing from God for all people, especially those who strive in His cause; it is divine generosity even though he built it.
rows.anchor: وفيه إيذان بأنه ليس من قبيل الآثار الحاصلة بمباشرة الخلق عادة بل هو إحسان إلهي محض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s promise means the Day of Judgment together with its precursors, including Gog and Magog, the Dajjal, and Jesus’ descent; God will flatten the sturdy barrier to level ground.
rows.anchor: والمراد بمجيئه ما ينتظم مجيئه ومجيىء مباديه من خروجهم وخروج الدجال ونزول عيسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading may mean flat ground or something flattened; whatever was raised and then spread is leveled, showing divine power after mercy. God’s promised events will certainly occur.
rows.anchor: وكل ما انبسط بعد ارتفاع فقد اندك وفيه بيان لعظم قدرته تعالى

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The inward commentary says Dhu al-Qarnayn’s confident report that the promise is true indicates prophethood, since this certainty and its miracle belong to prophets.
rows.anchor: دلالة على نبوته فإنه أخبر عن وعد الحق وتحقيق وعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A transmitted account says Gog and Magog dig daily but God restores the barrier until a believer tells them to return tomorrow, God willing; they then break through, kill and eat people, drain rivers and Lake Tiberias, fail to enter four sacred mosques, and attack toward Jerusalem.
rows.anchor: قيل : إن يأجوج ومأجوج يحفرون السد كل يوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report continues: Jesus and companions pray on Mount Sinai; worms kill Gog and Magog at once, birds carry away their corpses, and Muslims burn their bows, arrows, and quivers for seven years.
rows.anchor: فيرسل الله عليهم دودا تسمى النغف فتأخذهم في رقابهم
